vehicles.h1: Ford F-150 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: Reviewers rank the F-150 first among full-size pickups, and the one to price is a 2026 XLT. Ford has $4,500 cash on it through November 30 in most regions, and the average XLT sells 5–7% under MSRP before that. Watch the options: a typical XLT SuperCrew 4x4 stickers in the mid-$50,000s or higher. The 2027 has no incentives yet.

faq: Is the Ford F-150 a good truck?

Reviewers think so. Edmunds rates the 2026 an 8.0 out of 10 and first of five large trucks, and U.S. News ranks it first of six full-size pickups. Owners report harsh shifts from the 10-speed automatic, and 2021 and 2022 trucks have long recall lists.
How much under MSRP can you get a Ford F-150?

On a 2026 XLT or Lariat, 5–7% under MSRP is fair and about 10% strong, give or take a point or two. That’s our read of TrueCar’s November sale prices, which may include Ford’s cash. Count it as extra only if the quote itemizes it.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 F-150?

The 2026, for most buyers. It carries Ford’s year-end offers and dealers want it gone now that 2027s are arriving. The 2027 makes sense if you want the new 3.0L engine or the lower starting price on Lariat, Tremor or Raptor.
What is the destination charge on an F-150?
$2,795 on most 2026 trucks and on the 2027. Ford’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and it’s on every window sticker. A few early 2026 trucks show $2,595.
Can I combine 0% financing with the $4,500 cash back?
Plan on no. Ford’s 0% and 1.9% offers come with $500 or $1,500 in bonus cash, and the full $4,500 appears only as a cash offer. Ask the dealer to price the truck both ways in writing.
Is the F-150 hybrid worth it?

Only if you’ll use the onboard generator. It loses value faster than the gas truck by iSeeCars’ figures, and the early hybrids scored poorly for reliability with Consumer Reports. Consumer Reports now predicts about average reliability for the 2026.
Is a used F-150 a better deal than new?

Not by much right now. A three-year-old F-150 has lost about 19% of its value, against 25% for the average vehicle, and used loans averaged 11.19% against 6.35% for new. A Gold Certified 2023 or 2024 is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.h1: Toyota RAV4 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The RAV4 is hybrid-only now and still easy to recommend: 43 mpg combined with front-wheel drive, and it loses value about half as fast as the average vehicle. The catch is price. Toyota offers no cash back, and TrueCar’s averages put most trims within 2% of sticker. Price a 2026 XLE Premium and aim for 1–2% under MSRP.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Toyota dealers put add-ons on 37.7% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,637. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
Markups. Some dealers added $1,104 to $4,700 over sticker when the 2026 launched. Supply is still tight, so walk away from a markup and ask the next dealer.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The 4.99% and the $500 rebates need Toyota’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Fees. Documentation fees on RAV4 quotes ran from $180 in Iowa to $1,094 in Florida in CarEdge’s study. Compare out-the-door prices.
The plug-in recall. Ask the dealer to show that recall 26V659’s software update is done before you take delivery.
faq: Is the Toyota RAV4 a good SUV?

Most reviewers think so. Edmunds rates the 2026 an 8.1 out of 10, third of 12 small hybrid SUVs, and J.D. Power’s owner score of 85 ties it for first among compact SUVs. U.S. News is cooler, at 8.3 and 14th of 19 hybrid SUVs.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota RAV4?

On a 2026 LE, SE or XLE Premium, 1–2% under MSRP is fair and 3–4% strong. The Woodland, XSE and Limited sell at about sticker. That’s our read of TrueCar’s and Edmunds’ figures, so a dealer may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 RAV4?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $400 to $755 less, and Toyota’s 4.99% financing and $500 rebates apply only to the 2026. Wait for the 2027 if you want a plug-in with DC fast charging or the Woodland’s retuned suspension.
What is the destination charge on a RAV4?
$1,595 on the 2026 and the 2027, hybrid or plug-in. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and Toyota says it may differ in AL, AR, FL, GA, LA, MS, NC, OK, SC and TX.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the RAV4?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 15, 2026, Toyota offered 4.99% financing for 48 months and leases, with no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military or college rebate on a Toyota Financial Services loan or lease.
Is the RAV4 plug-in hybrid worth it?

Only if you can charge at home and most of your trips are short. The SE is EPA-rated for 54 miles on electricity, and Edmunds got 58 in testing. It costs $5,400 more than an AWD hybrid SE, and the federal tax credit is gone.
Is a used RAV4 a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $32,299, and TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 LE is $32,951. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Toyota’s 4.99%. A Gold Certified 2023 to 2025 hybrid is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.h1: Honda CR-V price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: Honda says the CR-V is America’s best-selling SUV this year, and it’s one of the easier small SUVs to buy below sticker: buyers on CarWhere paid a median 5.7% under MSRP. The 2027 is the same car for $400 to $600 more. Price a 2026 Sport Hybrid, aim for 2–5% under, and check Honda’s financing on a 2027.

intro: Our take: buy new, and price both model years. A leftover 2026 is the same car for $400 to $600 less, but Honda’s low rates are only on the 2027. A used CR-V barely costs less than a new one, and used-loan rates average 11.19%.

rows.when: You find one at 5% or more under MSRP, or you’re paying cash or bringing your own loan.
rows.check: That it’s a 2026, which Honda’s rates and leases don’t cover, and that the price beats a 2027 on Honda’s rate in total.

rows.when: You’ll finance through Honda at 3.49% to 4.99%, or you want the widest choice of trims and colors.
rows.check: The $400 to $600 price rise and the $1,550 destination charge.

rows.when: You want a 2023 to 2025 with a warranty, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: HondaTrue Certified covers 2021 and newer cars under 80,000 miles: the powertrain to 7 years/100,000 miles from first sale, everything else 2 years past the new-car warranty. The hybrid battery is covered 8 years/100,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $27,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2023 to 2025, that steering recall 24V744 is done.

after: If you buy used, make 2023 the floor. That year began the current CR-V. NHTSA has an open investigation into 2017 to 2022 CR-Vs that brake hard on their own (1,294 owner complaints), and 2017 and 2018 turbo engines could dilute their oil with fuel.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Honda dealers put add-ons on 35.1% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,159. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look the same on the lot. Honda’s rates and leases apply only to the 2027, and the 2026 should cost less.
The Honda Financial Services requirement. The low rates and every $500 or $750 offer need Honda’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
First payment in 90 days. Interest still builds during those 90 days, so it isn’t a discount.
Fees. CarEdge puts the national median for dealer fees at $498. Compare out-the-door prices.
faq: Is the Honda CR-V a good SUV?

Most reviewers think so. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.0 out of 10 and Kelley Blue Book 4.8 out of 5. Edmunds is cooler, at 7.4 (7.7 for the hybrid), and faults the slow gas engine and short list of driver aids.
How much under MSRP can you get a Honda CR-V?

On a 2026 LX, EX or EX-L, 3–4% under MSRP is fair and 5–6% strong. Sport and TrailSport hybrids get 2–3%, the Sport-L and Sport Touring 4–5% or more. That’s our read of TrueCar, Edmunds and CarWhere figures, give or take a point.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 CR-V?

Price both. Honda changed only the price for 2027: $600 more on the LX, $400 on the rest and $100 more for destination. A leftover 2026 should cost less, but Honda’s 3.49% to 4.99% financing and its leases are only on the 2027.
Should I wait for the 2028 CR-V?
Only if you want the new one. Honda says an all-new, hybrid-only CR-V arrives in 2027, but it hasn’t given a price or a date. The current CR-V is a known car that dealers are discounting now.
What is the destination charge on a CR-V?
$1,450 on the 2026 and $1,550 on the 2027. Honda’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and premium paint adds $455.
Does Honda offer cash back on the CR-V?

No. In the four regions we checked on November 16, 2026, Honda offered financing from 3.49%, leases from $299 a month and $500 for Honda owners, all on the 2027, with no customer cash. Military members and recent graduates get $500 on either year.
Is the CR-V Hybrid worth it?

For most buyers, yes. The Sport Hybrid costs $230 more than a gas EX-L and is rated 40 mpg combined against 30 with front-wheel drive. You give up the EX-L’s leather and power tailgate, and it loses value a little faster.
Is a used CR-V a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $33,066, more than TrueCar’s $31,517 average paid for a new 2026 LX. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026. A HondaTrue Certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. Sierras lose value faster than the average pickup, which makes a used one tempting. But a 2026 sells 5–7% under sticker this month, and used loans average 11.19% against 6.35% for new.

rows.check: That the truck is a 2026, which engine it has, and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $40,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 6.2L V8, proof that recall 25V274’s engine inspection was done.

after: Buying used? Start at 2023. The 2019 and 2020 trucks carry 10 and 12 recalls, and 2021 to 2024 trucks with the 6.2L V8 were recalled in 2025 for defects that can wreck the engine. Owners are suing GM over lifter failures on its V8s.

watch: Which engine. GMC’s cash and 0% apply only to the 3.0L Duramax, and you get one or the other. Make sure a quote names the engine.
Dealer add-ons. GMC dealers put them on 36.4% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,441. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products: refuse or negotiate them.
Fees. Documentation fees run from about $85 in California to $999 in Florida, by CarEdge’s count. Compare out-the-door prices.
The 6.2L V8. On a 2021 to 2024 truck, ask for proof that recall 25V274’s inspection was done. NHTSA’s open investigation also covers 2025 and 2026 engines.
The transfer case recall. A few 2026 4WD trucks are under recall 26V289 and shouldn’t be driven until fixed. Have the dealer check the VIN before delivery.
faq: Is the GMC Sierra 1500 a good truck?

Reviewers split on it. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.0 out of 10 and Kelley Blue Book 4.3 out of 5. Edmunds gives it 6.7, faulting the ride and fuel economy. Consumer Reports expects it to be less reliable than the average new car.
How much under MSRP can you get a GMC Sierra 1500?

On a 2026 SLE, Elevation or SLT, 5–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 8–10% a strong one. The Pro has less room, about 2–3%. That’s our read of TrueCar’s averages and iSeeCars’ invoice figures. GMC’s diesel cash comes on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Sierra 1500?

The 2026, unless you want the new truck. It costs less (the Denali starts $4,800 lower), the SLE and SLT exist only as 2026s, and GMC’s cash and 0% are on the 2026 diesel. The 2027 brings new V8s and a redesigned cabin.
What is the destination charge on a Sierra 1500?
$2,795 on the 2026 and the 2027. GMC’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does GMC offer cash back on the Sierra 1500?

Only on the diesel. On November 16, 2026, GMC offered $8,250 on a 2026 Sierra 1500 with the 3.0L Duramax, or 0% for 60 months plus $2,000. Gas 2026 trucks got lease deals only. The offers end November 30.
Is the Sierra’s 6.2L V8 reliable?

It has a record. GM recalled nearly 600,000 2021 to 2024 trucks and SUVs with the 6.2L in 2025, and NHTSA has since opened a wider investigation covering 2021 to 2026 engines. Until that closes, we’d take the 5.3L V8 or the diesel.
Is the Sierra 1500 the same truck as the Silverado?

They’re closely related and offer the same four engines. The Sierra costs more (the 2026 Pro starts at $38,600, against $37,200 for a Silverado WT) and is finished a step higher inside. Price both and let the better deal decide.

intro: Our take: buy new. The 2026 for the price, the 2027 if you want the better truck. Silverados lose value faster than the average pickup, but a 2026 sells 5–7% under sticker with $6,000 cash or 0% on top. Used loans average 11.19% against 6.35% for new.

rows.when: Most buyers. The runout discounts and Chevrolet’s cash and 0% are on the 2026, and the RST and LTZ exist only as 2026s.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026, which engine it has (the $6,000 needs the 5.3L), and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.when: You want the new 5.7L or 6.6L V8, the 16.3-inch screen and the redesigned cabin, or the 13,700-pound tow rating. Edmunds scores it 7.7 against 6.1 for the 2026.
rows.check: The price rise ($8,500 on the High Country, $900 to $1,400 on the Custom and WT), and that Chevrolet lists no 2027 offers yet.

rows.when: You want a 2023 to 2025 truck with some cover, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: CarBravo’s certified warranty is 12 months/12,000 miles bumper to bumper on trucks under 10 model years and 100,000 miles. Chevrolet’s powertrain warranty runs 5 years/60,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $37,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 6.2L V8, proof that recall 25V274’s engine inspection was done.

after: Buying used? Start at 2023. The 2019 and 2020 trucks carry 10 and 12 recalls, and 2021 to 2024 trucks with the 6.2L V8 were recalled in 2025 for defects that can wreck the engine. Owners are suing GM over lifter failures on its V8s.

watch: Which engine. The $6,000 applies only to the 5.3L V8 and the $2,250 only to an LT with the TurboMax. Make sure a quote names the engine.
Cash or 0%. You get one or the other. Work out the total cost of each with your bank’s rate before you choose.
Dealer add-ons. Chevrolet dealers put them on 32.4% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,443. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products: refuse or negotiate them.
The 6.2L V8. On a 2021 to 2024 truck, ask for proof that recall 25V274’s inspection was done. NHTSA’s open investigation also covers 2025 and 2026 engines.
The transfer case recall. A few 2026 4WD trucks are under recall 26V289, and GM tells owners not to drive them until fixed. Have the dealer check the VIN.
faq: Is the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 a good truck?
Reviewers are lukewarm on the 2026 and warmer on the 2027. U.S. News scores the 2026 an 8.8 out of 10 and Kelley Blue Book 4.3 out of 5. Edmunds gives it 6.1 and the redesigned 2027 a 7.7.
How much under MSRP can you get a Chevrolet Silverado 1500?

On a 2026 LT, RST, Custom Trail Boss, LTZ or LT Trail Boss, 5–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 8–10% a strong one. That’s our read of TrueCar’s averages and iSeeCars’ invoice figures. Chevrolet’s cash comes on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Silverado 1500?

The 2026 if price matters most. It costs less (the High Country starts $8,500 lower), and Chevrolet’s cash and 0% are on the 2026. The 2027 brings new V8s and a redesigned cabin, and Edmunds scores it 7.7 against 6.1 for the 2026.
What is the destination charge on a Silverado 1500?
$2,795 on the 2026 and the 2027. Chevrolet’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Chevrolet offer cash back on the Silverado 1500?

Yes, on the V8. On November 16, 2026, Chevrolet offered $6,000 on a 2026 Silverado 1500 with the 5.3L V8 and $2,250 on an LT with the TurboMax, or 0% for 60 months. All of it ends with delivery by November 30.
Is the Silverado’s 6.2L V8 reliable?

It has a record. GM recalled nearly 600,000 2021 to 2024 trucks and SUVs with the 6.2L in 2025, and NHTSA has since opened a wider investigation covering 2021 to 2026 engines. Until that closes, we’d take the 5.3L V8 or the diesel.
How much can a Silverado 1500 tow?

Chevrolet lists up to 13,300 pounds on the 2026 and up to 13,700 on the 2027 with the new 5.7L V8. A specific truck’s limit depends on its engine, cab, axle ratio and hitch, so check the trailering rating on its own label.
Is the Silverado 1500 the same truck as the Sierra?

They’re closely related and offer the same four engines. The Silverado costs less (the 2026 WT starts at $37,200, against $38,600 for a Sierra Pro) and is finished a step lower inside. Price both and let the better deal decide.

vehicles.summary: The Tacoma is the midsize pickup that holds its value best: iSeeCars puts its five-year depreciation at 19.5% against 30.2% for the class. Edmunds and U.S. News both fault the tight back seat. It still sells under sticker. Price a 2026 TRD Sport, aim for 5–6% under MSRP, and take Toyota’s 3.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it.

watch: Add-ons. In Florida, Georgia, Alabama and the Carolinas, Toyota’s regional distributor fits its own packages. One buyer reported $2,857 of them plus $1,599 from the dealer. Refuse or negotiate them.
Dealer stickers above Toyota’s. Some dealers print their own price over Toyota’s: one buyer saw $2,838 added to a TRD Off-Road. Negotiate down from Toyota’s window sticker.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. In Chicago and Dallas, only the 2026 has offers.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The 3.99%, the leases and the $500 rebates need Toyota’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Fees. Documentation fees in owner reports ran from $225 to $899. Compare out-the-door prices.
faq: Is the Toyota Tacoma a good truck?

Most reviewers think so. Kelley Blue Book rates the 2026 a 4.8 out of 5 and first among midsize trucks, and U.S. News gives it 8.8. Edmunds is cooler at 6.8, faulting the cramped back seat and engine noise under hard acceleration.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Tacoma?

On a 2026 SR5, TRD PreRunner, TRD Sport or TRD Off-Road, 5–6% under MSRP is a fair deal and 7–8% a strong one, by our read of TrueCar, Edmunds and CarWhere figures. The SR and the hybrids have less room, around 2–4%.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Tacoma?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $180 to $520 less, and nearly all of Toyota’s offers are on it: 3.99% financing, the SR5’s $500 finance cash and the leases. The 2027 gets 4.99% in Southern California and the New York area only.
What is the destination charge on a Tacoma?
$1,745 on the 2026. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $32,545 SR is $34,290 on the window sticker.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Tacoma?

No. On November 16, 2026, Toyota offered financing from 2.99% and lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is $500 on a 2026 SR5 financed through Toyota in three regions, and a $500 military or college rebate.
Is the Tacoma i-FORCE MAX hybrid worth it?
Only if you want its power or its 2,400-watt outlet. It makes 326 hp and 465 lb-ft against 278 hp and 317 lb-ft, but it costs $3,720 more on a TRD Sport 4x4 and is rated 23 mpg combined against 21.
Is a used Tacoma a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2024 is $38,119, while TrueCar’s average paid for a new SR5 starts at $36,274. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Toyota’s 3.99%. A Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.

rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified, not Silver. Gold adds a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage; Silver gives 12 months of powertrain cover only. A hybrid’s battery stays covered for 10 years/150,000 miles from first sale.

after: If you buy used, skip the 2020. It drew 316 NHTSA owner complaints, more than any Corolla since, and needed a stalling fix and a fuel pump recall. Check any used Corolla’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Toyota dealers put them on 37.7% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,637. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products: refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The 2027 costs $200 more, and its ToyotaCare covers one year or 10,000 miles against two.
Toyota financing. The 4.99% and the $500 rebates need Toyota Financial Services. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
The wrong hybrid. An AWD Hybrid SE is rated 44 mpg combined against 50 for a front-drive Hybrid LE. Check the window sticker if fuel economy is why you’re buying.
The headlight recall. NHTSA recall 26V110000 covers 2026 Corollas with incorrectly aimed headlights. Ask the dealer to show it’s done before you take delivery.
faq: Is the Toyota Corolla a good car?

Reviewers split. U.S. News scores it 8.6 out of 10 and KBB 4.5 out of 5, while Edmunds rates it 6.0 and ninth of 10 compact sedans. Consumer Reports expects it to be more reliable than the average new car.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Corolla?

On a 2026 gas LE or SE, 5–6% under MSRP is fair and 7% or more strong. Hybrids sell closer to sticker, so 3–4% is fair. That’s our read of TrueCar and CarWhere figures, so a dealer may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Corolla?
The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $200 less with the same engines and keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare maintenance, which Toyota cut to one year or 10,000 miles for the 2027.
Is the Corolla Hybrid worth it?

For most buyers, yes. A Hybrid LE costs $1,850 more than a gas LE and is rated 50 mpg combined against 35, about 100 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. Toyota covers the hybrid battery for 10 years or 150,000 miles.
What is the destination charge on a Corolla?
$1,295 on the 2026 and the 2027, sedan, Hybrid, Hatchback or GR Corolla. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and Toyota says it’s higher in AL, AR, FL, GA, LA, MS, NC, OK, SC and TX.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Corolla?

No. On November 16, 2026, Toyota offered 4.99% financing for 48 months and lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military or college rebate when you finance or lease through Toyota Financial Services.
How much is a GR Corolla?

The 2026 starts at $40,520 with the manual and $42,520 with the automatic, and the Premium Plus is $46,565 and $48,565, all before the $1,295 destination charge. Edmunds found it selling about $1,500 under sticker in November.
Is a used Corolla a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2025 asks a median $22,016 at about 34,000 miles, and TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 LE is $22,665 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Toyota’s 4.99%. A Gold Certified 2021 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

faq: Is the Honda Civic a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.4 out of 10, first of eight compact cars. Edmunds rates the gas Civic 6.9 and the hybrid 7.9, its 2026 Top Rated Car.
How much under MSRP can you get a Honda Civic?

Less than most compact cars. On a 2026 LX or Sport, 2–3% under MSRP is fair and 4–5% strong. On hybrids, 1–2% is fair and 3–4% strong. That’s our read of Edmunds, CarWhere and iSeeCars figures, and a dealer may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Civic?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $300 less with the same engines, and Honda’s 3.99% financing covers only the 2026, through November 30. Buy the 2027 if you want the new gas Sport-L or S+ Shift on the Sport Touring Hybrid.
Is the Civic Hybrid worth it?

Yes, for most buyers. A Sport Hybrid sedan costs $2,700 more than a gas Sport and is rated 49 mpg combined against 34, about 110 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. It’s also much quicker and adds heated seats and a moonroof.
What is the destination charge on a Civic?
$1,295 on the 2026 and the 2027, for every Civic including the Si and Type R. Honda’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and the $455 premium paint charge is extra too.
Does Honda offer cash back on the Civic?

No. On November 16, 2026, Honda offered 3.99% financing on the 2026 and leases on both years, but no customer cash. Honda owners get $500 on the sedans, and military buyers and graduates $500 on every Civic, all through Honda Financial Services.
Is Honda still making the Civic Si?
Not for 2027. Honda lists no 2027 Si, so the 2026 ($31,495 plus $1,295 destination, six-speed manual only) is the last one for now. It has no special financing or lease from Honda.
How much is a Civic Type R?

The 2026 is $47,395 and the 2027 $48,695, both before the $1,295 destination charge. Markups have mostly gone: Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase price for a 2026 is $48,100, a little under the $48,690 sticker with destination.
Is a used Civic a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2025 asks a median $25,575 at about 29,500 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LX is $25,508 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Honda’s 3.99%. A HondaTrue Certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

watch: Open recalls. Run the VIN at NHTSA. The headlight recall on 2020–2023 cars (26V507) has no fix yet, and the suspension, seat and steering wheel recalls need a service visit.
The front suspension. NHTSA opened an investigation in July 2026 into front lateral links failing on 2021–2023 Model Ys. Have an independent shop look at it before you buy.
Hardware 3. Most cars built before mid-2023 have Hardware 3, which Tesla says can’t run unsupervised FSD. If a listing charges for FSD, check the car’s screen shows it.
The “warranty” on the window. A dealer’s warranty is its own or a third party’s. Tesla’s used warranty covers only cars Tesla sells. Ask for the first delivery date.
Door handles on a 2021. NHTSA is investigating 2021 Model Ys whose outside handles stop working when the 12-volt battery runs low. Ask when that battery was last replaced.
faq: How much is a used Tesla Model Y?

Dealers listed them at an average of $26,400 for a 2020 up to $39,700 for a 2025 in September 2026, by Recurrent’s count. Each 10,000 miles takes about $1,000 off. A new Model Y starts at $39,990 before $1,640 in fees.
How much under asking can you get a used Model Y?

On a 2023 to 2025, 1–2% under asking is fair and 3–4% strong. On a 2020 to 2022, about 1% is fair and 2–3% strong. Those ranges are our estimate: used Model Ys sell in about 16 days, so dealers rarely cut much.
What is the best year for a used Model Y?

The 2024, in our view. It was built after the switch to Hardware 4, has five recall campaigns against 17 to 24 for the 2020 to 2023, and battery cover that runs into 2032. A 2023 built after mid-year is next, at about $3,300 less.
Does the Tesla battery warranty transfer to a used buyer?
Yes, at no cost, whoever sells you the car. It runs 8 years or 120,000 miles on a Long Range or Performance and 8 years or 100,000 miles on a Standard or Standard Range, counted from first delivery.
Does a used Model Y from a dealer come with Tesla’s warranty?

Not Tesla’s used warranty. Its 1-year/10,000-mile cover applies only to used cars Tesla sells and delivers itself. The remainder of the original 4-year/50,000-mile basic warranty and the battery warranty do carry over.
Does Full Self-Driving transfer with a used Model Y?

Tesla says FSD bought outright stays with the car. It now sells FSD only as a subscription, which doesn’t carry over. Check that FSD shows on the car’s own screen before you pay extra for it. Tesla says Hardware 3 cars can’t run unsupervised FSD.
Is a used Model Y reliable?

Mixed. U.S. News predicts 78 out of 100. Owners of three-year-old Teslas reported 226 problems per 100 vehicles in J.D. Power’s 2026 dependability study, against an industry average of 204, and Germany’s TÜV failed 17.3% of two- to three-year-old Model Ys at inspection.

vehicles.summary: The Camry is the midsize sedan most buyers should start with, and every one is a hybrid: a front-drive LE is rated 51 mpg combined. Edmunds and U.S. News both find the engine coarse when you push it. Edmunds’ Texas prices run about 7–8% under sticker. Price a 2026 XLE and aim for 4–5% under MSRP.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Toyota dealers put add-ons on 37.7% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,637. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products: refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike. The 2027 costs $100 more, and its ToyotaCare covers one year or 10,000 miles against two years or 25,000.
The inverter recall. NHTSA recall 25V869 covers some 2025 and 2026 Camrys. A loose inverter bolt can cut power or cause a fire. Ask for proof the inverter was replaced.
Toyota financing. The 4.99% and the college rebate need Toyota Financial Services. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Which year the rate covers. Toyota’s 4.99% was on the 2027 only in Chicago and the 2026 only in Los Angeles. Ask which model year the dealer’s quote assumes.
faq: Is the Toyota Camry a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.4 out of 10, first of nine hybrid cars. Edmunds rates it 8.4 and Kelley Blue Book 4.8 out of 5 with its Best Buy Award.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Camry?

On a 2026 LE, SE or XSE, 5–6% under MSRP is a fair deal and 7% or more a strong one. The Nightshade and XLE are harder to find, so 4–5% is fair. That’s our read of Edmunds, CarWhere and iSeeCars figures.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Camry?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $100 less with the same engine and equipment, and it keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare. Buy the 2027 if Toyota’s 4.99% covers only the 2027 in your region, as it did in Chicago.
Is every Camry a hybrid?

Yes, since the 2025 redesign. Every Camry has a 2.5-liter four-cylinder hybrid with 225 hp, or 232 hp with AWD. The EPA rates the front-drive LE at 51 mpg combined and the other front-drive trims at 46.
Is AWD worth it on a Camry?
If you see snow, yes. It adds $1,525 on every trim and costs little in fuel: the EPA rates an AWD SE or XLE at 46 mpg combined, the same as front drive. The AWD XSE drops to 43.
What is the destination charge on a Camry?
$1,295 on the 2026, up from $1,195 on the 2025. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Camry?
No. On November 17, 2026, Toyota offered 4.99% financing for 48 months and lease deals in the four regions we checked, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military or college rebate.
Is a used Camry a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2025 asks a median $27,989 at about 40,000 miles, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LE is $28,450 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Toyota’s 4.99%. A Gold Certified 2022 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

after: Buying used? Make 2023 the floor. NHTSA has an open investigation into 2018 to 2022 Accords that brake hard on their own. On a 2024 or 2025, ask about the steering: owners have filed 128 NHTSA complaints about it, and there’s no recall.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Honda dealers put add-ons on 35.1% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,159. On a $35,000 Accord that’s most of a 3% discount. Refuse or negotiate them.
The January 4 deadline. Honda’s 3.49–3.99% financing, the leases and the $750 owner offer all end January 4, 2027.
A scarce EX-L. Edmunds says EX-L Hybrid stock is tight. The Sport-L Hybrid has the same leather and power seats for $400 more, so don’t pay over sticker.
Honda financing. The low rates and the $500 offers need Honda Financial Services. Interest still builds during “No payments for 90 days.” Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Recalls on a used one. Ask for proof that fuel pump recall 24V763 is done on a 2023 or 2024, and software recall 25V785 on a 2023 to 2025 Hybrid.
faq: Is the Honda Accord a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.5, first of four midsize cars. Edmunds rates it 8.3, second of six midsize sedans behind the Toyota Camry. NHTSA gives it five stars in every test.
How much under MSRP can you get a Honda Accord?

On an LX, SE or Sport Hybrid, 2–3% under MSRP is fair and 4–5% strong. On an EX-L or Sport-L Hybrid, 3–4% is fair, and on a Touring Hybrid, 4–5%. That’s our read of TrueCar, Edmunds and CarWhere figures. Honda adds no cash back.
Is the Accord Hybrid worth it?

Yes, for most buyers. An EX-L Hybrid costs $4,400 more than a gas SE and is rated 48 mpg combined against 31, about 135 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. It loses value a little faster: 22.1% in three years by iSeeCars’ count.
Is there a 2027 Honda Accord?
Not in the U.S. yet. On November 17, 2026, Honda listed only the 2026 and hadn’t announced a 2027 price. Edmunds lists a 2027 as upcoming. The 2026 is the one to price now.
What is the destination charge on an Accord?
$1,295 on every 2026 Accord. It was $1,195 when the 2026 launched, which is why some sites still show a $29,590 starting price. With today’s charge an LX is $29,690.
Does Honda offer cash back on the Accord?

No. On November 17, 2026, Honda offered 3.49–3.99% financing and leases on the 2026 but no customer cash. Honda owners get $750. Military buyers and recent graduates get $500 through Honda Financial Services.
Should I buy an Accord or a Toyota Camry?

Price both. The Camry is hybrid-only, starts at $29,600, offers all-wheel drive and is an IIHS Top Safety Pick+, and Edmunds rates it the better car. The Accord has the bigger discounts and a gas version from $28,395. See our Camry price guide.
Is a used Accord a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2025 asks a median $28,124 at about 17,700 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LX is $29,018 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Honda’s 3.99%. A HondaTrue Certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.summary: The Tundra is the full-size pickup for buyers who want a smooth twin-turbo V6, a roomy cab and strong resale, and who don’t need the biggest tow rating. Edmunds measured 15.2 mpg on its test route. Most trims sell 5–7% under sticker. Price a 2026 Limited and take Toyota’s 1.99% to 2.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used 2024 asks a median $44,714, only about $1,200 under what TrueCar says buyers pay for a new SR5 ($45,885). Used loans average 11.19% against Toyota’s 1.99% on a new hybrid.

rows.when: Most buyers. Toyota’s financing, the $1,000 cash and the leases apply to the 2026, it costs $640 to $4,530 less than a 2027, and its ToyotaCare covers two years or 25,000 miles.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026 and not a 2027, and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.when: The 2026 you want is gone, or you want the 14-inch touchscreen and built-in dash camera Toyota makes standard for 2027.
rows.check: The price rise, that its 3.99% and $1,000 cash run only in Southern California and the New York area, and that ToyotaCare drops to one year or 10,000 miles.

rows.when: You want a 2024 or 2025 with a warranty, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified (7 years or 100,000 miles of powertrain cover from purchase), not Silver (12 months or 12,000 miles), and that every engine recall is done. A hybrid battery stays covered for 10 years or 150,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $40,000; a 2022 asks a median $39,079.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, above all the engine campaigns (main bearings on 2022 to 2024 trucks, a camshaft on 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026 trucks), and an independent inspection.

after: If you buy a 2022 to 2026 Tundra, get the engine recall work in writing. Main-bearing recalls cover certain 2022 to 2024 trucks, and camshaft recall 26V750 covers 2022 to 2023 and 2025 to 2026 trucks. Both fixes are free.

watch: Engine recalls. Four NHTSA campaigns cover 2022 to 2026 trucks: three for main bearings and 26V750 for a camshaft. Ask the dealer to show each applicable one is done.
Toyota financing. The rates and leases need Toyota Financial Services, and the $1,000 cash doesn’t combine with them. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. In Chicago and Dallas only the 2026 has offers.
Fuel economy. Edmunds measured 15.2 mpg on its test route against the EPA’s 19 for a 4WD Tundra. Budget for the real figure if you tow or drive in town.
Towing and payload. Toyota’s top figures are 12,000 pounds and 1,850 pounds. Check the rating for your exact cab, bed and engine on the door sticker.
faq: Is the Toyota Tundra a good truck?

Mostly yes, with caveats. U.S. News gives the 2026 a 9.0, third of six full-size pickups, and J.D. Power’s owner score is 82. Edmunds is cooler at 7.0, fourth of five large trucks, and faults its fuel economy, thick front pillars and mid-pack towing.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Tundra?

On a 2026 SR through 1794 Edition, 5–7% under MSRP is fair and 8–9% strong. The TRD Pro sells near sticker, around 3–4%. That’s our read of TrueCar, Edmunds and CarWhere figures. Toyota’s $1,000 cash comes on top, but not with its low rates.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Tundra?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $640 to $4,530 less, nearly all of Toyota’s offers are on it, and its ToyotaCare runs two years against one. The 2027 adds a standard 14-inch touchscreen and a built-in dash camera.
What is the destination charge on a Tundra?
$2,195. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $41,260 SR is $43,455 on the window sticker.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Tundra?

Yes: $1,000 customer cash on 2026 gas and i-FORCE MAX trims, except the TRD Pro, in all four regions we checked on November 18, 2026. It doesn’t combine with Toyota’s 1.99% or 2.99% financing or its leases.
Is the Tundra i-FORCE MAX hybrid worth it?

Only if you want its power. It makes 437 hp and 583 lb-ft against 389 hp and 479 lb-ft, adds $3,700 to a Limited and is rated 20 mpg combined against 19 in 4x4. Toyota’s 1.99% reaches it in all four regions we checked.
Is a used Tundra a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2024 asks a median $44,714, while TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 SR5 is $45,885. Used loans averaged 11.19% against 1.99% on a new hybrid. A Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 with engine recalls done is the used route we’d take.

after: Buying used? A 2022 to 2025 is safer than a 2019 or 2021. NHTSA logged 277 complaints on the 2019 and 150 on the 2021 (134 and 81 about the engine), against 66 for the 2022. Check any used CX-5’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Offers that don’t stack. Mazda’s $1,000 customer cash can’t be combined with its special APR or lease. Ask for the price with each and compare the totals.
The model year. A 2026 and 2027 look alike on the lot. The 2027 costs $150 to $550 more above the base, and the 0% is on the 2026.
Touchscreen controls. Touchscreen controls replaced the physical buttons, Edmunds says. Try the climate and cruise controls on a test drive.
The data plan. Google built-in is free for one year, then needs a monthly subscription. Edmunds says $15.
The destination charge. Mazda’s is $1,595. Edmunds and Kelley Blue Book print $1,495, so check the window sticker against any quote.
faq: Is the Mazda CX-5 a good car?

Reviewers split. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.3 out of 10, first of 14 compact SUVs. Edmunds rates it 6.5, 14th of 20 small SUVs, and calls it less engaging to drive than before. IIHS lists it as a Top Safety Pick+.
How much under MSRP can you get a Mazda CX-5?

On an S, Select or Preferred, 4–5% under MSRP is a fair deal and 6% or more a strong one. On the Premium and Premium Plus, 3–4% is fair. That’s our read of Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book and CarWhere figures. Mazda’s $1,000 cash is separate.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 CX-5?

The 2026, for most buyers. It has the same engine and equipment for $150 to $550 less on every trim above the base, plus Mazda’s 0% APR and customer cash. Buy the 2027 if Mazda’s rate covers only the 2027 where you live.
Is there a CX-5 hybrid?
Not yet. Every 2026 and 2027 CX-5 has a 2.5-liter four-cylinder. Mazda says additional powertrain options will be announced in 2027, and Edmunds expects a hybrid to arrive then.
What mpg does the CX-5 get?
The EPA rates every 2026 CX-5 at 26 mpg combined (24 city/30 highway). All-wheel drive is standard, so there’s no front-drive version to compare.
What is the destination charge on a CX-5?
$1,595 ($1,640 in Alaska) on the 2026 and 2027. Mazda’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and Edmunds and Kelley Blue Book still print $1,495.
Does Mazda offer cash back on the CX-5?
Yes. On November 18, 2026, Mazda offered $1,000 customer cash on a 2026 S, Select or Preferred in Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York. It can’t be combined with Mazda’s special APR or lease.
Is a used CX-5 a better deal than new?

Only if you want to spend under about $24,000. A used 2025 asks a median $26,669 at about 30,500 miles, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 2.5 S is $29,875 with destination. The used 2025 is also the smaller, previous-generation CX-5.

faq: Is the Ram 1500 a good truck?

For comfort, yes. Edmunds gives the 2026 a 7.5 out of 10 and says it rides more comfortably than any rival. U.S. News gives it 9.5, second of six full-size pickups. Edmunds scored its reliability 3 out of 10.
How much under MSRP can you get a Ram 1500?

On most 2026 trims, 8–10% under MSRP is a fair deal and 12% or more a strong one. The Laramie to Tungsten group runs 7–9%, and the RHO about 5–6%. That’s our estimate, so a dealer may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Ram 1500?
The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $400 to $1,200 less, and Ram’s cash and 0% financing apply to it through November 30. The 2027 gets employee pricing and a 5.9% rate in Chicago.
What is the destination charge on a Ram 1500?
$2,795 on both years. Ram’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $42,025 Tradesman is $44,820 on the window sticker.
Does Ram offer cash back on the 1500?

Yes, on the 2026. In Chicago, Dallas and New York it’s $1,500 to $5,250 depending on trim, with $6,000 on a Big Horn Crew Cab 4x4. Los Angeles pays up to $6,750. The 0% financing replaces the cash, and the 2027 shows none.
Is the V8 or the turbo six better?

The six. In Edmunds’ tests the 420-hp six reached 60 mph in 5.2 seconds and the 395-hp V8 in 6.9, and Edmunds calls the six quieter and cheaper. Kelley Blue Book calls the V8 the gem of the line on towing and price.
Is a used Ram 1500 a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2024 asks a median $37,898 and a 2025 $40,566, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new Big Horn is $42,883. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Ram’s 0%. A certified 2023 to 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.description: What a Hyundai Elantra costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for the gas, Hybrid and N, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Hyundai’s current offers, and the trim we’d buy.
vehicles.h1: Hyundai Elantra price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Elantra is the value play against the Civic and Corolla: it starts $1,870 below a Civic LX, the Hybrid Blue is rated 54 mpg combined, and it sells about 6% under sticker. The base engine is slow and the cabin is loud at speed. A redesign is due in 2027, so the 2026 is the last of this design.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used one barely costs less: the median used 2025 asks $21,235, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 SE is $22,700 with destination, before Hyundai’s $2,000. Used loans average 11.19% against Hyundai’s 3.49%.

rows.when: Most buyers. It gets the $2,000 bonus cash, 3.49% financing and the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty.
rows.check: That Hyundai’s cash and rate cover the trim you want (the Hybrid and N get less), and that recalls 26V692000 (front struts) and 26V693000 (wheel bearings) are done.

rows.when: You don’t need a car before 2027 and want the new design, a larger screen and the redesigned hybrid.
rows.check: That Hyundai hasn’t announced U.S. prices or an on-sale date, and that a new design usually costs more than a closeout.

rows.when: You want a 2021 to 2026 with a warranty. Hyundai’s 5.99% helps.
rows.check: That it’s Certified Used, not Select Used. Certified adds a 173-point inspection, 5 years/60,000 miles of comprehensive cover and a transferable 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty from first sale; Select Used gives only 90 days or 5,000 miles of powertrain cover.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $17,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and the engine on a 2019 or 2020 (the top complaint category on both).

after: Buying used? Look at a 2023 or newer. The 2019 and 2020 drew 253 and 255 NHTSA owner complaints, with engine problems leading the list, against 118 for the 2023. Check any used Elantra’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Dealer add-ons. CarWhere found them on 34.1% of the quotes it studied, averaging $1,454. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products: refuse or negotiate them.
The wheel and strut recalls. NHTSA recalls 26V693000 (lug nuts that may loosen) and 26V692000 (front strut fasteners) cover some 2026 Elantras. Ask the dealer to show both are done.
Which trims the cash covers. The $2,000 is for the gas Elantra. The Hybrid gets $500 and the N none.
Hyundai financing. The college rebate needs Hyundai Motor Finance, and in Dallas so does the $2,000. Compare the total with your bank’s rate.
Wireless CarPlay. It comes only with the 8-inch screen. The 10.25-inch screen needs a cable, Edmunds found.
faq: Is the Hyundai Elantra a good car?
For value, yes. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.0 out of 10 and Kelley Blue Book 4.6 out of 5. Edmunds gives the gas car 6.8, finding the base engine slow and the cabin loud, and the Hybrid 7.6.
How much under MSRP can you get a Hyundai Elantra?

On a gas SE through Limited, 3–4% under MSRP is a fair deal and 5–6% a strong one. That’s our read of Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book and iSeeCars figures, so a dealer may land a point either side. Hyundai’s $2,000 cash comes on top.
Is the Elantra Hybrid worth the extra money?

If you drive a lot. A Hybrid Blue costs $1,700 more than a gas SEL Sport and is rated 54 mpg combined against 34, about 130 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. This month the gas car gets the bigger offer.
Does the Hyundai Elantra have a redesign coming?
Yes. Hyundai showed the next Elantra in South Korea in June 2026, and it’s expected in U.S. showrooms in 2027. There are no U.S. prices yet, so the 2026 is the current car.
What is the destination charge on an Elantra?
$1,295 on the 2026. Hyundai’s advertised starting prices leave it out: the SE’s $22,825 is $24,120 with destination.
Does Hyundai offer cash back on the Elantra?
On the gas car, yes: $2,000 bonus cash through November 30, checked November 18, 2026. The Hybrid gets $500 and the N none. Military buyers and recent graduates get $500.
Is the Elantra N worth buying?
Edmunds ranks it first of four sport compacts, and it starts at $35,300, less than a GR Corolla ($40,520) or Civic Type R ($47,395). See the Elantra N section above.
Is a used Elantra a better deal than new?

Rarely this month. A used 2025 asks a median $21,235, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 SE is $22,700 with destination, before $2,000 of Hyundai cash. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Hyundai’s 3.49%.

spotlight.heading: Elantra N: the 276-hp one
intro: The Elantra N is a different car: a 276-hp turbo four, a six-speed manual or eight-speed dual-clutch, and a limited-slip differential. Edmunds ranks it first of four sport compacts (7.1 out of 10). The catches are a braced trunk, no adaptive cruise control and above-average road noise.

watch: The ball-joint recall. Recall 26V685 covers some 2026 Foresters. Subaru says not to drive an affected car until it’s fixed. Ask for the repair in writing.
Which engine you test-drive. Edmunds finds the gas Forester slow and its engine coarse and noisy when pushed. Drive the hybrid and a gas car back to back.
The gas Premium’s option package. The Premium Hybrid’s power rear gate and blind-spot detection are a $1,200 package on a gas Premium. Add it before you compare.
The 2027’s changes. The 2027 has a $1,525 destination charge, costs more as a gas Limited or Wilderness, and loses the gas Sport and Touring. Check which year you’re quoted.
The credit conditions. Subaru’s rates are for well-qualified buyers and need delivery from retailer stock by November 30. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
faq: Is the Subaru Forester a good car?

Reviewers like it but don’t agree how much. U.S. News scores the 2026 8.6 out of 10 and J.D. Power owners give it 84 out of 100. Edmunds rates it 5.7 and calls the gas engine slow. IIHS names it a 2026 Top Safety Pick+.
How much under MSRP can you get a Subaru Forester?

About 5–6% on most 2026 trims, and 7% or more on a strong deal. That’s our read of Edmunds, CarWhere and iSeeCars figures, so a dealer may land a point either side. On the Base and Sport Hybrid, 4–5% is fair. Subaru offers no cash.
Is the Forester Hybrid worth it?

For most buyers, yes. A Premium Hybrid costs $2,735 more than a gas Premium and is rated 35 mpg combined against 29. Edmunds says it’s noticeably quicker. It still trails an AWD Toyota RAV4 hybrid (41 mpg combined) and an AWD Honda CR-V hybrid (37).
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Forester?

The 2026, for most buyers. Subaru’s financing is on the 2026, destination is $75 less, and the Base, Premium and hybrid trims cost the same either year. Buy the 2027 if you want the new Wilderness Hybrid ($40,495).
Is the Forester good off-road?

More than most small SUVs. Every Forester has all-wheel drive and at least 8.7 inches of ground clearance. The Wilderness sits 9.3 inches up, with all-terrain tires, a full-size spare and a 3,500-pound tow rating. Other Foresters tow 1,500 pounds.
What is the destination charge on a Forester?
$1,450 on the 2026 ($1,600 in Alaska) and $1,525 on the 2027 ($1,675 in Alaska). Subaru’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Subaru offer cash back on the Forester?
No. On November 18, 2026, Subaru listed 1.99% and 3.99% financing and two lease deals in the four regions we checked, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military discount.
Is a used Forester a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2025 asks a median $31,476 at about 15,000 miles, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 Premium is $31,124 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Subaru’s 1.99% or 3.99%. A Subaru Certified Forester is the used route we’d take.

after: Buying used? Look at a certified 2023 to 2025 and ask for the recall paperwork. The 2023 and 2024 were recalled for a camera fault that could trigger automatic emergency braking by mistake, overtightened front wheel hub bolts and a loose seat belt buckle bolt.

watch: Brakes. NHTSA is running an engineering analysis (EA26006) into loss of brake assist, and the 2023 to 2026 Colorado is on its list. No recall as of November 18, 2026.
Cash or rate. Chevrolet doesn’t say whether the $1,000 cash and the 4.9% rate combine. Ask for a quote each way and compare the total cost.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot, and the cash and financing are on the 2026.
The back seat and storage. U.S. News calls the back seat tiny, and Edmunds scores storage 3 out of 10. Try both on the lot.
Fees and add-ons. Dealers add fees and extras to the price you see online. Compare out-the-door prices, and refuse or negotiate anything you didn’t ask for.
faq: Is the Chevrolet Colorado a good truck?

Good, though short of the top. Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.6 out of 5 and U.S. News 8.7. Edmunds is cooler at 6.5 and faults the rear seat and storage. Consumer Reports expects it to be less reliable than the average new car.
How much under MSRP can you get a Chevrolet Colorado?

On a 2026 WT, Custom or LT, 6–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 9–10% a strong one. The ZR2 has less room, around 5–6%. That’s our read of Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book and iSeeCars figures, so dealers may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Colorado?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $100 to $1,200 less, and Chevrolet’s 4.9% financing and customer cash are on the 2026. The 2027 has a 350-hp engine against 310, which matters if you tow near the 7,700-pound limit.
What is the destination charge on a Colorado?
$2,095 on both model years. Chevrolet’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $32,400 WT is $34,495 on the window sticker.
Does Chevrolet offer cash back on the Colorado?

Yes, to November 30: $1,000 customer cash on a 2026 ($500 on the Trail Boss and ZR2), $1,000 for eligible military members and $2,000 conquest cash for owners of a Tacoma, Ranger or five other rival models. Chevrolet’s page doesn’t say which combine.
Should I buy a Colorado or a Tacoma?

The Colorado if you tow: Edmunds says its towing, payload and screen lead the class. The Tacoma if resale matters most. It loses 19.5% of its value in five years against the Colorado’s 36.9%, iSeeCars says.
Is a used Colorado a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2024 asks a median $36,087, while a new 2026 LT starts at $36,000 and sells 6–7% under that. Chevrolet’s 4.9% financing compares with 11.19% for the average used loan. A certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

Yes, as bonus cash through November 30, 2026: up to $3,000 on the gas Tucson, $1,750 on the Hybrid and $4,000 on the Plug-in. On the gas SEL Premium and Limited it requires Hyundai Motor Finance and goes toward the down payment.
Is a new Hyundai Tucson coming?

Yes. Hyundai’s site lists an all-new Tucson and Tucson Hybrid for early 2027, with no U.S. price or mpg yet. The 2026 is the last of the current generation, introduced for 2022 and refreshed for 2025.
What is the destination charge on a Tucson?
$1,650, per iSeeCars. That matches Hyundai’s own fine print on a Hybrid Night ($44,575 including destination against a $42,925 sticker). Hyundai’s MSRPs leave it out.
Is AWD worth it on a Tucson?
If you see snow. It adds $1,500 on the gas Tucson and the Hybrid SE and SEL, and costs about 2 mpg combined. The Hybrid SEL Convenience, Limited, Night and both plug-ins come with it.
Is a used Tucson a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2025 asks a median $24,493, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 SE is $29,201. Hyundai finances the new one at 0% or 2.9% against 11.19% on average for used loans. A used 2023 or 2024 is the value play.

vehicles.summary: The Ranger is the midsize pickup to price first if ride quality and tech matter to you. Edmunds ranks it first of seven midsize trucks. intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used 2024 asks a median $37,075, about what a new XLT costs before Ford’s $2,500 cash. Used loans average 11.19% against Ford’s 4.9% on a new one.

rows.check: That the offer runs in your region, that the truck is not a Raptor if you expect the bonus cash, and that its recalls are done.

rows.when: You can wait, or you want the 2027’s changes.
rows.check: Ford has not posted 2027 prices or offers on ford.com, and the 2027 lineup may swap the 2.7L V6 for a 3.0L V6, per a report on Ford’s order guide.

rows.when: You want a 2024 or 2025 with a warranty and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: That it is Gold Certified, not Blue. Gold covers trucks up to 6 years old with under 80,000 miles, adds a 172-point inspection, a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage. Blue Certified gives 90 days or 4,000 miles.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $31,000, which buys a 2023 or older.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and that you are comparing like with like: the Ranger was redesigned for 2024, so a 2023 is the previous generation.

after: Buying used? A Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 is the route we’d take. Ask for the recall paperwork in writing: NHTSA lists 13 recall campaigns on the 2024 and 13 on the 2025. A 2023 is the previous generation.

watch: Engine recalls. Two NHTSA recalls cover loss of drive power: 26V343 (2025–2026, a new engine long block) and 26V548 (2026, an inspection). Check any truck’s VIN before you sign.
Rearview camera recall. 26V605 covers 2026 Rangers with the 10.1-inch screen, which can lose power and drop the camera image. NHTSA lists the remedy as under development.
Dealer-installed extras. Ford’s own price list shows a hard roll-up tonneau cover at $1,470 and cargo management rails at $600. Ask for extras you didn’t request to come off.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 can sit on the same lot. Ford’s current offers are for the 2026.
Cash or rate. The 4.9% needs Ford Credit approval, and Ford’s pages do not say whether it combines with the cash. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
faq: Is the Ford Ranger a good truck?

Most reviewers say yes, with one outlier. Edmunds scores the 2026 a 7.1 out of 10, first of seven midsize trucks, and Kelley Blue Book 4.7 out of 5. U.S. News ranks it seventh of seven, faulting low-speed transmission jitters and cheap cabin materials.
How much under MSRP can you get a Ford Ranger?

On an XL, XLT or Lariat, 3–4% under MSRP is a fair deal and 6–7% a strong one, before Ford’s $2,500 cash. The Raptor has less room, around 1–2%. Those ranges are our read, so a dealer may land a point either side.
What is the destination charge on a Ranger?
$1,895 on the 2026. Ford’s advertised prices leave it out, so a $33,550 XL is $35,445 on the window sticker.
Does Ford offer cash back on the Ranger?

Yes, until November 30, 2026: $2,000 customer cash plus $500 Black Friday bonus cash on a 2026 Ranger. The bonus cash is not available on the Raptor. Ford’s pages do not say whether the cash combines with its 4.9% financing, so ask the dealer.
Should I buy the 2.7L V6?

Probably not. Edmunds clocked a V6 Ranger at 6.2 seconds to 60 mph against 6.7 for a four-cylinder Lariat 4x4, and the EPA rates it 20 mpg combined against 21. Both engines tow 7,500 pounds with the Trailer Tow Package.
Is the Ranger Raptor worth it?
Only if you will use it off pavement. It starts at $57,270 against $43,955 for a Lariat, is rated 17 mpg combined and tows 5,510 pounds against 7,500. It gets none of Ford’s November cash.
Is a used Ranger a better deal than new?

Rarely. A used 2024 asks a median $37,075, while a new XLT starts at $36,075 before Ford’s $2,500 cash. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Ford’s 4.9%. A Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.

watch: Open recalls. Run the VIN at NHTSA. The headlight repair for 2017–2023 cars (26V507) isn’t available yet. 2025 cars need a service visit for battery-pack contactor recall 25V690.
Hardware 3 or 4. Every 2017–2023 Model 3 has Hardware 3, which Tesla says can’t run unsupervised FSD. The 2024 has Hardware 4. Check under Settings, Software, Additional Vehicle Information.
FSD in the listing. Tesla says FSD bought outright stays with the car, and now sells it only as a subscription. Check it’s on the car’s screen before paying extra.
The “warranty” on the window. A dealer’s warranty is its own or a third party’s. Ask for the first delivery date to see how much battery cover is left.
Suspension, brakes and lights. Germany’s TÜV failed 13.1% of two- to three-year-old Model 3s, against about 6.5% for that age group. Have an independent shop inspect the car first.
faq: How much is a used Tesla Model 3?

An average of $21,100 for a 2019 up to $38,200 for a 2025 at dealers in September 2026, by Recurrent’s count. Each 10,000 miles takes about $1,000 off a car of the same year. A new Model 3 starts at $36,990 before fees.
How much under asking can you get a used Model 3?

On a 2024 or 2025, 1–2% under asking is fair and 3–4% strong. On a 2019 to 2023, about 1% is fair and 2–3% strong. That’s our estimate: nobody publishes used Model 3 sale prices. Tesla doesn’t negotiate on its own used cars.
What is the best year for a used Model 3?

The 2023 Long Range AWD, in our view: about $9,500 below the average 2024 asking price, with 358 miles of EPA range. Buy a 2024 or later if you want Hardware 4, the quieter cabin and ventilated front seats.
Does the Tesla battery warranty transfer to a used buyer?

Yes, at no cost, from any seller. It runs 8 years or 120,000 miles on a Long Range or Performance and 8 years or 100,000 miles on a Standard or Standard Range Plus, counted from first delivery, and covers capacity that falls below 70%.
Does a used Model 3 from a dealer come with Tesla’s warranty?

Not Tesla’s used warranty. Its 1-year/10,000-mile cover applies only to used cars Tesla sells and delivers itself. The remainder of the original 4-year/50,000-mile basic warranty and the battery warranty do carry over.
Does Full Self-Driving transfer with a used Model 3?

FSD bought outright stays with the car, Tesla says. A subscription, the only way Tesla sells it now, doesn’t carry over. Check FSD shows on the car’s screen before paying extra. Tesla says Hardware 3 cars can’t run unsupervised FSD.
Is a used Model 3 reliable?

Mixed. U.S. News predicts 82 out of 100 for the 2026. Owners of three-year-old Teslas reported 226 problems per 100 vehicles in J.D. Power’s 2026 dependability study, against 204 for the industry. Germany’s TÜV failed 13.1% of two- to three-year-old Model 3s at inspection.

rows.when: Most buyers. It costs $100 to $200 less than the 2027 and carries 0% for 48 months and $750 customer cash.
rows.check: That Kia’s rate covers the car you’re buying, that a hybrid S or EX is the AWD you want (the 2026 had no front drive), and that recall 26V046 is done.

rows.when: You want a front-drive hybrid S or EX (new for 2027), or a gas X-Line with the sunroof and liftgate standard.
rows.check: The $100 to $200 price rise, and that the 0.90% (hybrid) or 1.99% rate is the one in your quote.

rows.when: You want a 2023 or newer Sportage with a warranty.
rows.check: That it’s certified, not just used. Kia’s terms are a 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty and 1 year or 12,000 miles of Platinum coverage after a 165-point inspection. Ask for the age and mileage limits in writing.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $24,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2023 that its seven recalls are done.

after: If you buy used, look at a 2024 or 2025 and be wary of a 2020 or 2023. The 2020 drew 172 NHTSA owner complaints, 81 about the engine. The 2023 drew 212 and seven recalls; the 2024 drew 77 and the 2025 56.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Kia dealers put add-ons on 43.3% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,477. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products: refuse or negotiate them.
The model year and the rate. The 0% is for a 2026. A 2027 gas Sportage gets 1.99% and a 2027 hybrid 0.90%. Ask which year the quote assumes.
AWD-only 2026 hybrids. A 2026 hybrid S or EX is AWD only, at 35 mpg combined against 42 for the front-drive LX. A 2027 comes in front drive at 41.
Specially tagged cars. Kia’s $750 Retail Bonus Cash on a gas 2026 Sportage is for specially tagged vehicles only. Ask the dealer to show the tag.
The instrument panel recall. Recall 26V046 covers 2026 Sportages, Hybrids and Plug-ins: a software error can make the instrument panel display fail. Ask if the free fix is done.
faq: Is the Kia Sportage a good car?

Reviewers rank it near the top of its class, with a caveat about the gas engine. U.S. News scores the 2026 gas Sportage 8.9 out of 10, third of 14 compact SUVs. Edmunds rates the gas car 7.8 and the hybrid 8.6.
How much under MSRP can you get a Kia Sportage?

On a 2026 gas Sportage, 4–5% under MSRP is fair and 6% or more strong. On a hybrid LX, S, EX or X-Line, 3–4% is fair and 5–6% strong. That’s our read of Edmunds, TrueCar and CarWhere figures. Kia’s cash is separate.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Sportage?
Price both. A 2026 costs $100 to $200 less on most trims, carries 0% for 48 months and $750 customer cash, and sells further under sticker. A 2027 hybrid S or EX comes in front drive, at 0.90%.
Is the Sportage Hybrid worth it over the gas Sportage?
For most buyers, yes. A 2027 hybrid LX costs $1,600 more than a gas LX and is rated 41 mpg combined against 28, with 232 hp against 187. The EPA puts its fuel cost at $1,450 a year against $2,150.
Is AWD worth it on a Sportage?
If you see snow, yes. On the gas Sportage it adds $1,800 and costs 2 mpg (26 combined against 28). On a hybrid it costs more fuel: 35 mpg combined against 41 or 42 for front drive.
What is the destination charge on a Sportage?
$1,495 on both the 2026 and the 2027, up from $1,395 at the 2026 launch. Kia’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Kia offer cash back on the Sportage?

Yes. On November 18, 2026, Kia listed $750 customer cash on a 2026 Sportage or Sportage Hybrid and $500 on a 2027 Sportage Hybrid, plus $750 Retail Bonus Cash on a 2026 hybrid or plug-in. All end January 4, 2027.
Is a used Sportage a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $28,319, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LX is $28,870 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% against Kia’s 0% on a new 2026. Kia Certified Pre-Owned is the used route we’d take.

intro: Our take: buy new. There’s no used e-POWER Rogue yet, and Nissan’s 4.9% on a new Hybrid beats the 11.19% used-loan average. A used 2025 gas Rogue asks a median $21,464 at about 42,600 miles against $29,490 for a new 2026 S, and Nissan’s cash narrows that gap.

rows.when: You want the quiet, quick one and can take the SR Technology now or wait for the SV, SR and Platinum in January.
rows.check: The exact trim, price and delivery month in writing, and that Nissan’s 4.9% covers the trim you’re quoted.

rows.when: Payment comes first. The 2026 has 0% for 60 months and $4,500 on a Platinum; the 2027 has $3,000 cash or 2.9% in some regions.
rows.check: The model year, whether the cash or the rate applies (Nissan’s cash can’t be combined with its special rate or lease), and engine recalls 25V437 and 26V080.

rows.when: You want a 2021 to 2026 gas Rogue with a warranty; Nissan offers 4.99% for up to 36 months on a 2021 or newer Certified Rogue.
rows.check: Certified means up to 6 years old with under 80,000 miles, a 167-point inspection and a 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain limited warranty, for gas-powered models (Nissan doesn’t say whether a hybrid qualifies).

rows.when: Your budget is under about $20,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, proof that the engine software updates were done, and an independent inspection.

after: On a used gas Rogue, lean to a 2025 or 2026. The 2023 drew 784 NHTSA complaints, more than 400 about the engine, and 2021 to 2025 Rogues with the 1.5-liter VC-Turbo are on engine-bearing recalls. Nissan says the Hybrid’s 1.5-liter is a different engine.

watch: Which Hybrid you’re quoted. Only the SR Technology ($43,065 with destination) is on lots now. Get the trim, price and delivery month in writing before a deposit.
The 38 mpg. It’s Nissan’s estimate until the EPA rates the car, and Edmunds lists 37 for the SV and Platinum. Check the window sticker.
Cash or the rate. On a gas Rogue, Nissan’s cash can’t be combined with its special rate or lease, so price both.
Accessories. Hybrids arrive with port-installed extras such as $470 floor mats and a $795 lighting package. You can refuse or negotiate them.
faq: How much is the Nissan Rogue Hybrid?
From $35,490 for the SV to $43,490 for the Platinum, all with AWD, plus $1,575 destination. Edmunds says buyers are getting about $1,200 off.
How many mpg does the Rogue Hybrid get?

Nissan estimates 38 mpg combined (41 city/36 highway) for the SR, pending EPA confirmation. Edmunds lists 37 for the SV and Platinum, and its test SR returned 42.2 mpg. The gas Rogue is rated 30 with front drive and 29 with AWD.
When does the Rogue Hybrid go on sale?
Now, as the $41,490 SR with the Technology Package. The SV, SR and Platinum are due in January 2027.
What is e-POWER, and do I plug it in?

No plug. The 1.5-liter turbo engine only charges the battery, and two electric motors drive the wheels, so there’s no transmission. Nissan covers the hybrid system and battery for 8 years/100,000 miles.
What does Reddit think of the Rogue Hybrid?

In the 41 threads about the new Hybrid and the plug-in, people like the power and the quiet, but call a first-year hybrid unproven and pricier than a RAV4 Hybrid. Across all Rogues, most complaints are about CVT and 1.5-liter turbo failures on older cars.
Is the Rogue Hybrid worth it over the gas Rogue?

For most buyers, yes. A Hybrid SV costs $3,400 more than an AWD gas SV and brings 225 hp against 201, 37 to 38 mpg against 29, and an 8.2 Edmunds score against 6.4. The gas Rogue starts at $29,690 with $3,000 of Nissan cash.
How much under MSRP can you get a Nissan Rogue?
On a Hybrid, 2–3% under is a fair deal and 4% or more a strong one. On a gas Rogue, 4–5% is fair and 6% or more strong, before Nissan’s cash. Our estimate from Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book and CarWhere.

spotlight.heading: Rogue Hybrid: Nissan’s first e-POWER car in the U.S.
intro: Nissan’s first e-POWER car in the U.S. The 1.5-liter turbo engine only charges the battery, and two electric motors, one per axle, drive the wheels for 225 hp. No plug, no transmission.
